subject: Architecture review / technical deep-dive — scheduling + pre-read
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Sara Hall <sara.hall@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Architecture review / technical deep-dive — scheduling + pre-read

Hi team,

Per our conversations last week, Acme has asked for a technical deep-dive around the proposed integration pattern and runtime architecture. I want to schedule a 60–90 minute architecture review (slides + diagrams + Q&A) with their eng/infra leads.

Proposed windows (PDT):
- Thu 2026-06-04, 10:00–11:30
- Fri 2026-06-05, 13:00–14:30

High-level agenda I’m thinking:
1) 10m — intros & goals
2) 25–30m — Redwood serving runtime architecture (layers, routing, caching)
3) 20–25m — Acme integration pattern & proposed configuration (VPC/private deployment options)
4) 15–20m — open QA and next steps / action items

Marissa/Markus — can you confirm availability for either window and whether you can share the pre-read slides + a diagram of the KV cache and routing flows? Ideally we can send pre-reads 48h before the session.

Sara — are either of the above times workable for Acme? Also let me know any particular topics you want emphasized (e.g., audit logs, KMS integration, latency SLOs).

I’ll assemble a short pre-read pack and meeting agenda once we lock time.

Thanks,
Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Sara Hall <sara.hall@acme.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Architecture review / technical deep-dive — scheduling + pre-read

Hi Lauren —

Either slot works for me; I prefer Jun 4 if we want to get this done sooner. I’ve attached a draft pre-read and the KV/cache diagram. The slides include the runtime overview and a section on recommended quantization/profile options for the Acme workload.

Attachments: pre-read-slides.pptx (pptx, 6.1MB); kv-cache-diagram.png (image/png, 420KB)

Notes on content:
- Slide 6: routing policies (latency tier vs cost tier) — we should confirm which policy Acme expects in prod.
- Slide 9: rollout & rollback plan for model variants — includes fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is unavailable.

I’ll add a short appendix with the sequence diagram for request flow through the cache and routing layer.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Sara Hall <sara.hall@acme.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Eng Architecture Team <eng-arch@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Architecture review / technical deep-dive — scheduling + pre-read

Hi Lauren / team,

Thanks — we’re keen to do this. Unfortunately Jun 4 at 10:00 conflicts with an internal planning meeting. Jun 5 13:00—14:30 would work for most people, but one of our infra leads (J. Alvarez) is only available 14:00–15:30 that day.

Could you do Jun 5 14:00–15:30 PDT instead? If that’s not possible, we can push to Mon 2026-06-08 morning.

Also the pre-read looks great at a glance; could you include a short section on audit logging and how traces map to customer request identifiers? That’s a key ask from our security team.

Best,
Sara

Sara — thanks for the note and the availability detail. Jun 5 14:00–15:30 PDT works for us; I’ve updated the calendar invite (placeholder) and locked the slot.

Final agenda (60–90 min; we’ll schedule 90 to allow extra Q&A):
- 14:00–14:10 — Intros, goals, success criteria (Lauren)
- 14:10–14:40 — Redwood serving runtime deep-dive (Marissa) — includes routing, KV cache behavior, and fallback model variants
- 14:40–15:00 — Proposed Acme integration and deployment options (Markus) — VPC/private control-plane flow, KMS/HSM notes
- 15:00–15:20 — Security & audit logging discussion (Lauren + Marissa) — how request IDs/trace IDs map through the system, retention, and access controls
- 15:20–15:30 — Action items & next steps

Pre-reads (in Drive):
- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-pre-read-slides (pre-read-slides.pptx)
- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1d4e5f-kv-diagram (kv-cache-diagram.png)
- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1g7h8i-arch-overview (architecture-overview.pdf)

I’ve added a 2-slide appendix on audit logging and trace mapping per Sara’s ask — see slides 14–15. Marissa, please take a quick pass and confirm.

Meeting invite will include the above links and the Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Acme+Integration+Architecture+Review

Thanks all — looking forward to the session.

Lauren

Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
